title: Alembic cross-repository interface contract independent demand sequence
philosophy: Each item is an independent demand definition. State roots are created one at a time when total control claims the next demand. Order is dependency order, not parent/subtask hierarchy.
globalUserDecisions: Version and long-term evolution strategy are deferred for D0-D7.
This is optimization, not feature reduction; preserve full existing functionality.
Do not accept thin minimum implementations, placeholder adapters, docs-only shells, static mocks, narrow demos, or happy-path-only evidence.
Delete fields, endpoints, events, adapters, or compatibility paths only after no-consumer proof, replacement evidence where needed, and representative validation.
Preserve only compatibility that has a real current consumer, currentCompatibilityOwner, validation evidence, and cleanup blocker.
Consumers must use explicit capability discovery instead of guessing provider support.
Ordinary outputs may include only public and consumer-needed fields; diagnostic fields require diagnostic context; internal, sensitive, or unrelated derived fields must not leak.
Large logs, reports, snapshots, long diagnostics, and replay payloads use compact summaries plus detailRef or artifactRef.
Test is not a default D0-D6 phase; use Test only if D7 still needs independent real runtime observation after product self-verification.

Total control may proceed unattended through D0-D7 unless scope expansion, deletion/downgrade, version/evolution need, functionality-preservation failure, sensitive-field ambiguity, repository-boundary conflict, or missing acceptance evidence occurs.
Product repository commits and evidence belong to owning product windows; root/Design/ledger docs and final acceptance belong to the controller.
claimRules: Claim at most one demand at a time.
Do not dispatch from this manifest alone.
This is optimization, not feature reduction; preserve existing functional behavior unless the user explicitly approves removal or downgrade.
Do not accept thin minimum implementations, placeholder adapters, docs-only shells, static mocks, narrow demos, or happy-path-only evidence as completion.
Do not design versioning, deprecation windows, remove-after dates, breaking-change policy, or long-term evolution strategy in this sequence.
D0 and D1 must record capability coverage, capability discovery, error kind, exposure class, artifact policy, fixture policy, drift gate, current compatibility owner, and observability keys.
D0 and D1 must be accepted before product-window implementation demands.
D4 and D6 must wait for accepted D3 provider evidence.
D7 must review raw evidence from D2-D6 before parent completion.

items.title: Full Cross-Repo Contract Inventory
items.goal: Create the complete evidence inventory for all cross-repository interfaces across AlembicCore, Alembic, AlembicPlugin, AlembicAgent, and AlembicDashboard before any implementation or cleanup.
items.completionDefinition: Every active cross-repo interface is inventoried with producer, consumer, primary functionClass, transport, schema source, validation seam, legacy duplicate status, preserved functional behaviors, capability discovery, error kinds, exposure classes, artifact policy, fixture source, drift gate candidate, current compatibility owner, observability keys, removal blocker, risk, and concrete repo-relative code references. Inventory alone is not implementation completion and cannot propose feature reduction without consumer/use-scan evidence and user/controller decision. Version/evolution fields are deferred.

initialTaskPackages.summary: Build the five-repo contract inventory and classify every package, REST, event, MCP, Agent, and Dashboard contract surface.
initialTaskPackages.targetSummary: Read the demand definition, inspect all five repositories read-only, and backfill the complete contract inventory evidence.

items.title: Contract Registry And Source-Of-Truth ADR
items.goal: Turn D0 inventory into a controller-visible contract registry and source-of-truth decision record for the five repositories.
items.completionDefinition: Registry and ADR define the producer-owned source of truth, functionClass handling rule, consumers, preserved capability coverage, capability discovery, error kinds, exposure classes, artifact policy, fixture policy, drift gate, current compatibility owner, observability keys, validation command, removal blocker, and security/property exposure notes for every contract layer. No handling rule may reduce existing behavior to a thin minimum path. Version/evolution strategy is deferred.

initialTaskPackages.summary: Create the contract registry schema, initial rows, and ADR from accepted D0 inventory evidence.
initialTaskPackages.targetSummary: Build the registry and ADR, preserving producer ownership and avoiding a central Core monolith.

items.title: AlembicCore Shared Deterministic Contract Spine
items.goal: Clean and verify Core-owned deterministic contracts, exports, validators, and boundary tests needed by real consumers.
items.completionDefinition: Core-owned contracts have stable public exports, validation, consumer evidence, preserved existing behavior, and boundary tests; Core does not absorb MCP, UI, AI provider, CLI daemon, or tool-execution responsibilities, and cleanup cannot narrow shared contracts to a thin import-only shell.

initialTaskPackages.summary: Implement and verify the Core shared deterministic contract spine from accepted registry rows.
initialTaskPackages.targetSummary: Read the state root and Core AGENTS, update only Core-owned deterministic contracts, and return tests and boundary evidence.

items.title: Alembic HTTP, Runtime, And Event Provider Contracts
items.goal: Make Alembic the checked provider for REST, runtime, job, and event contracts consumed by Dashboard and Plugin.
items.completionDefinition: Alembic provides checked OpenAPI or equivalent route schemas, an event manifest or typed registry, provider fixtures, and route/event tests for active consumer paths without leaking internal stores. Existing Alembic API/runtime/event behavior remains available through clean provider contracts, not reduced to easy success routes.

initialTaskPackages.summary: Implement and verify Alembic provider contracts for HTTP, runtime, jobs, and events.
initialTaskPackages.targetSummary: Read the state root and Alembic AGENTS, update only Alembic provider contracts, and return schema/event/route evidence.

items.title: AlembicPlugin Host, MCP, And Resident-Service Contracts
items.goal: Align Plugin MCP, host adapter, clean output, and resident-service contracts with accepted Core and Alembic provider evidence.
items.completionDefinition: Every active MCP tool has tool-specific input/output schema and projector behavior; resident-service client tests replay Alembic provider fixtures; no tool returns unrelated fields or preserves bad legacy compatibility without a recorded consumer and cleanup trigger. Existing host-facing Plugin capabilities remain available through clean per-tool contracts.

initialTaskPackages.summary: Implement and verify Plugin host/MCP/resident-service contract alignment.
initialTaskPackages.targetSummary: Read the state root and Plugin AGENTS, update only Plugin-owned contracts, and return MCP/resident-service evidence.

items.title: AlembicAgent Runtime, Tool, And Provider Contracts
items.goal: Clean and verify Agent runtime, tool, result-envelope, provider-adapter, and host-adapter contracts consumed by Alembic.
items.completionDefinition: Agent public contracts cover success, failure, cancellation, timeout, permission denial, partial result, provider errors, and host adapter paths without exposing provider internals as public runtime contracts. Existing Agent runtime/tool/provider behavior remains reachable and is not collapsed to a happy-path-only envelope.

initialTaskPackages.summary: Implement and verify Agent runtime/tool/provider contract alignment.
initialTaskPackages.targetSummary: Read the state root and Agent AGENTS, update only Agent-owned runtime/tool/provider contracts, and return tests and consumer evidence.

items.title: AlembicDashboard Consumer Contract And View-Model Cleanup
items.goal: Align Dashboard API client, event consumers, and view-model adapters with accepted Alembic provider contracts.
items.completionDefinition: Dashboard consumes checked provider schemas/fixtures, keeps frontend view models presentation-only, tests API/event consumers against provider fixtures, and preserves loading/empty/error/partial/unavailable states. Existing Dashboard user-visible behavior remains available after cleanup.

initialTaskPackages.summary: Implement and verify Dashboard consumer contract and view-model cleanup.
initialTaskPackages.targetSummary: Read the state root and Dashboard AGENTS, update only Dashboard consumer/view-model contracts, and return tests and UI evidence where needed.

items.title: Cross-Repo Acceptance, Drift Gates, And Legacy Cleanup
items.goal: Accept the full cross-repo interface contract cleanup with raw evidence, drift gates, deletion scans, validation matrix, and real runtime smoke where justified.
items.completionDefinition: All registry rows have producer evidence, consumer evidence, validation output, and deletion/compatibility status; cross-repo checks pass or are repaired; replaced duplicates are deleted only after import scans and representative validation; final acceptance covers CLI/daemon/API, Plugin MCP, Agent runtime/tool, and Dashboard consumer behavior. Final acceptance proves preserved functionality across representative success and non-success paths; no minimal happy-path implementation can close this demand.

initialTaskPackages.summary: Review all previous demand evidence, run drift/validation gates, close cleanup, and decide final acceptance.
initialTaskPackages.targetSummary: Build the final review pack, inspect raw evidence, run workspace verification, and create any Test card only if real runtime observation remains necessary.
